messages.author: de3b3fd8069924e2
messages.subject: F2 QTL Mapping - 1:2:1 - Why we remove distorded markers
parts:
Dear all,

I am doing QTLs analysis as well as Single Marker analysis as well.

I am wondering why we remove marker which deviate 1:2:1 segregation when we do QTL analysis ?


I also realized when I do single marker analysis showed strong statistical association. Is this something statistical artifact which linear model don't take into account ?


Any guidance/explainaion would be appreciated ?


Cheers

Kaz

messages.author: a10aec168f8330d3
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] F2 QTL Mapping - 1:2:1 - Why we remove distorded markers
parts:
Distorted markers should be removed cause it can lead to non causal or wrong statistical significance in QTL detection...

Single marker always should be done... The problem related to single marker QTL analyses it that the causal gene, most of the times, isn't the analysed marker. This fact happens, for exemple, when we consider genetic markers just like SSR, that for sure we know isn't a codant region. Significance in most cases is related to linkage effect between the analysed marker and the causal gene.

Most of the times, single marker analyses is pretty importante when we procede analyses just like CIM or procedure when we need associated markers as covariates, and they could be chosen taking a look at the results of single marker analyse...

It would be helpfull if someone could add some information or correct if I wrote something wrong or missplaced... 
I'm sorry for my English...

Best Regards
Rafael

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] F2 QTL Mapping - 1:2:1 - Why we remove distorded markers
parts:
I wouldn't remove markers deviation from 1:2:1 segregation in every case. I'd want to see whether the deviation from 1:2:1 was real segregation distortion or due to genotyping errors, and I'd omit the marker if I felt it was especially error-prone.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] F2 QTL Mapping - 1:2:1 - Why we remove distorded markers
parts:
Is it an isolated marker showing segregation distortion which all surrounding markers look fine (that would indicate genotyping error), or does an entire chromosome region show distortion in the same way (that would seem to be real).

In QTL mapping, we condition on the observed genotypes, so results are usually not much affected by real distortion, though can be some loss of power if some genotypes are only observed in a few individuals.

karl
